_readme: Example config for the flake -> CIF export & placement pipeline.
1. Leave everything at these defaults and run once against flakes/all/ (or your own
already-selected images) with --no-placement to check per-image CIFs look right.
2. Inspect cif_export_results.json — any image with status 'alert' was skipped, not
3. If real markers are being missed/rejected, adjust crosshair_core_min_area/max_area/min_extent,
If real flakes are missing from the output CIFs, lower
4. Confirm grid_pitch_um / placement_x_offset_um / placement_y_offset_um match your
actual marker grid and master template before trusting placement in production —
grid_pitch_um must equal the real-world spacing between adjacent grid letters
(e.g. AA to AB) on YOUR chip; do not trust a printed scale-bar overlay for this,
only the known real grid spacing.
5. Once happy, drop --no-placement and point --template at your real master CIF.
_comment_detection_config_path: DetectionConfig JSON reused for flake color range and marker pink/bright ranges — keep this in sync with whatever flake_detection used to find these images.
_comment_flake_detection_output_dir: A flake_detection run's own --output folder (contains contours/). If set, each image's flakes/<stem>.json in THIS run's output gets flake_detection's real per-flake contour+score, transformed through this image's own calibration -- what contact_placement consumes. Leave null to skip (flakes/<stem>.json will just be empty).
_comment_channel_selection: Runs the trained channels_model first: reconstructs a posterized image (unselected clusters -> a flat substrate-colored fill, selected clusters -> their real measured color) and feeds THAT into marker detection/calibration/polygon extraction instead of the raw original. channels_n_clusters/channels_cluster_median_win must match how channels_model_onnx_path was actually trained (see channels_model/outputs/effective_config.json). channels_cache_dir is deliberately its own folder, NOT channels_model's training cache -- filename collisions between the two image sets (same stem, different image) were confirmed empirically.
_comment_markers: Top-2 crosshair marker detection: find solid, squarish CORE-shaped blobs in the non-substrate mask alone (not the whole cross -- the 4 arms are the least color-stable part of a real image, see markers.py's own module docstring), then confirm each core candidate is really a crosshair (not a plain grid-dot square) via arm evidence in the real image -- crosshair_arm_min_count of its 4 arm directions must each have at least crosshair_arm_min_fraction non-substrate coverage. Finally refined per-image to the crosshair's actual solid-color square core by direct HSV color thresholding (marker_refine_color_hsv +-hue/sat tolerance, V unconstrained) within a small window. Works because marker detection now runs on the reconstructed image, where the core is a flat channels_model cluster color, not the noisy antialiased original. HSV (not RGB) because the same real-world crosshair color renders at a different RGB per batch/image due to lighting -- HSV isolates that mostly-brightness effect into V, which is left unconstrained, matching only on H/S. Tune the top group if real markers are being missed (widen crosshair_core_min_area/max_area/min_extent, or lower crosshair_arm_min_count/crosshair_arm_min_fraction) or noise is being picked up (tighten them). Tune the refine_* group if the refinement step is finding the wrong blob or falling back too often -- re-measure marker_refine_color_hsv from a new batch's own reconstructed/*.png (see markers.py) rather than just widening tolerance further.
_comment_placement: grid_pitch_um is the ONE real-world grid used both for marker-pair calibration (scale + rotation) and for placement (grid ID -> absolute position): confirmed 200um, e.g. AA to AB. X_um = placement_x_offset_um + col_idx*grid_pitch_um, Y_um = placement_y_offset_um - row_idx*grid_pitch_um.
_comment_polygon_export: Background/foreground is separated by edge detection (Canny), not color -- immune to the substrate's lighting gradient, which tripped up every color-based approach tried before this (fixed HSV threshold, k-means clustering). edge_blur_kernel denoises before edge detection; edge_canny_low/high are the Canny hysteresis thresholds; edge_close_kernel/iterations bridge small gaps so real content's edges form closed, fillable loops. Everything inside a closed loop (flakes, debris, AND the markers/scaling marks themselves) is exported, colored by its own measured mean color. gds_min_area filters out noise contours (px) before scoring; raise it if tiny specks are showing up as polygons. min_flake_score is an OPTIONAL quality-score threshold for THIS phase (same color/texture/isolation formula as flake_detection's min_final_score, but independent of it and NOT applied by default -- flake_detection's threshold only decides which images get reviewed; this one, if raised above 0.0, decides which regions within an image get exported). Start at 0.0 (everything), inspect cif_export_results.json's polygon_scores, then raise only if you want to start excluding low-scoring regions. max_vertex_n is the CIF polygon vertex cap (larger contours are recursively split).
_comment_color_palette: Each exported polygon is colored to match its own real channels_model cluster color (see polygons.py / channel_selection.py), not one fixed monocolor layer. flake_layer_palette seeds cif_io.LayerPalette; left empty deliberately -- the old 6 'Flake' layers (101-106) here were a fixed legacy thickness-gradient scheme that predates real per-cluster colors, and confirmed empirically to force wrong colors (a real cluster RGB(160,111,124) got silently overridden onto RGB(202,99,101)). Colors are quantized by palette_quantize_step and matched by EXACT quantized value only (no nearest-neighbor-radius merging -- an earlier version did that and let two genuinely different classes collide onto the same layer/color, confirmed empirically, e.g. the crosshair's own real color ~RGB(238,190,221) getting forced onto an unrelated layer). Only set flake_layer_palette if you want new colors to defer to some other pre-existing palette.
_comment_output: template_cif_path is only ever read, never modified in place -- it's copied once into --output and every placement is spliced into that working copy. Set to null to skip placement entirely (same effect as --no-placement).
